appliesTo: frontier developers (foundation models trained with >10^26 operations); heightened duties on large frontier developers (>$500,000,000 annual gross revenues)

dutySources.risk-program: § 10(a) — 'shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a frontier AI framework'
dutySources.documentation: § 10(c)(1) — 'a frontier developer shall clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a transparency report'
dutySources.impact-assessment: § 10(e) — 'A large frontier developer shall transmit to the Agency a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk resulting from internal use of its frontier models every 3 months'
dutySources.incident-reporting: § 15(c) — 'A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Agency and the Attorney General within 72 hours'
dutySources.registration-filing: § 18(a) — 'no large frontier developer may develop, deploy, or operate a frontier model, in whole or in part in this State, without having a current disclosure statement filed with the Agency and paying the required fee'

sources.threshold: § 5 — '"Frontier model" means a foundation model that was trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations'
sources.safetyFramework: § 10(a) — 'shall write, implement, comply with, and clearly and conspicuously publish on its website a frontier AI framework'
sources.incidentReporting: § 15(c) — 'shall report any critical safety incident pertaining to one or more of its frontier models to the Agency and the Attorney General within 72 hours'
sources.thirdPartyAudit: § 10(d) — 'shall annually retain a third party to perform an independent audit of compliance with the requirements of this Section'
sources.whistleblower: § 20(a) — 'A frontier developer shall not make, adopt, enforce, or enter into a rule, regulation, policy, or contract that prevents a covered employee from disclosing, or retaliates against a covered employee for disclosing'
sources.penaltyMax: § 25(a) — 'For a subsequent violation, the civil penalty may not exceed $3,000,000 per violation.'
sources.enforcer: § 25(b) — 'recovered in a civil action brought exclusively by the Attorney General'

flags: Two-tier scope: framework, third-party audit, quarterly internal-use risk summaries, and registration bind only 'large frontier developers' (>$500,000,000 revenue, § 5); transparency reports (§ 10(c)(1)), 72-hour incident reporting (§ 15(c)), and whistleblower non-retaliation (§ 20(a)) bind all frontier developers.
threshold=compute is lossy: the large-frontier-developer tier adds a revenue test (§ 5 — 'annual gross revenues in excess of $500,000,000 in the preceding calendar year').
§ 10(d) annual third-party audit is a compliance audit and fits no listed duty key (bias-audit is discrimination-specific); captured only via the thirdPartyAudit param.

penaltyMax codes the subsequent-violation cap; § 25(a) caps the first violation at $1,000,000, and § 18(e)(1) adds a separate 'civil penalty of $1,000 for each day' for registration/disclosure failures levied by the Agency.
§ 17 interoperability safe harbor: a developer declaring compliance with an Agency-designated substantially equivalent federal law/regulation/guidance 'shall be deemed in compliance with this Act'.
Sections 80 and 90 amend the Freedom of Information Act and the Whistleblower Act (non-company-duty provisions); § 18 duties begin January 1, 2027, § 10(a)/(d) duties begin January 1, 2028.
